source.title: Head-to-head comparative effectiveness of empagliflozin versus dapagliflozin and DPP-4 inhibitors on clinical and metabolic outcomes: a nationwide propensity-matched study

cross_batch_consistency_findings.main_source: Main Methods, PDF p.15: all-cause hospitalization, time to first hospitalization, irrespective of prior hospitalization history.
cross_batch_consistency_findings.supplement: Supplementary Table S1, p.1: "Diabetes-related hospitalisation (HOS)" = admission with primary diagnosis E11.x–E14.x.
cross_batch_consistency_findings.resolution: Not repaired. Both source statements are preserved; the exact implemented claims outcome cannot be established unambiguously from the supplied materials.

cross_batch_consistency_findings.main_source: Table 2 presents adjusted HRs under EMPA vs DAPA / EMPA vs DPP4i and the prose interprets HR <1 as lower risk with EMPA.
cross_batch_consistency_findings.figure: Figure 2 legend labels the same plotted values "DAPA vs EMPA" and "DPP4i vs EMPA".
cross_batch_consistency_findings.resolution: Not repaired. SEA treats Table 2/prose as the effect-direction interpretation and flags the figure legend as internally inconsistent.

cross_batch_consistency_findings.methods: Methods, PDF pp.13–14: exposure/new-user classification on or after January 1, 2016.
cross_batch_consistency_findings.figure: Figure 1, PDF p.30: antidiabetic drug exposure "since 2016.05".
cross_batch_consistency_findings.resolution: Not repaired. Both dates are reported as printed.

cross_batch_consistency_findings.main_source: Main Methods, PDF p.15 includes new-onset acute/chronic kidney disease, progression to advanced CKD, or initiation of dialysis.
cross_batch_consistency_findings.supplement: Supplementary Table S1, p.1 defines kidney event as incident acute kidney injury or advanced CKD and supplies N17.x/N18.x/N19 codes; no dialysis procedure code is shown.
cross_batch_consistency_findings.resolution: Not repaired. The supplement appears narrower/less explicit than the main-text definition.

extraction_limitations: The source is an accepted, unedited article-in-press manuscript; copyediting may change the final version.
No causal effect is inferred from the observational associations.
The supplied supplement was included as source material; no unprovided supplemental artifacts were assumed.
